query: What drives customer satisfaction (Overall Rating) across the different airlines?

per_column.name: Average_Service_Rating
per_column.rationale: This is the mean of the sub-rating dimensions (Seat Comfort, Staff Service, Food & Beverages, Inflight Entertainment, Value For Money). Overall Rating is effectively a summary of these same dimensions, so this is a near-deterministic aggregate of the focus rather than an independent predictor.

per_column.name: Service_Consistency
per_column.rationale: The standard deviation across the same sub-rating dimensions used to form the overall rating. It is a derived function of the ratings that constitute the outcome, so it restates in-focus information rather than supplying external signal.

per_column.name: Lowest_Rated_Dimension
per_column.rationale: Derived directly from the component sub-ratings that determine the overall rating. Knowing which dimension is lowest is a function of the same rating vector, so it leaks the outcome.

per_column.name: Poor_Dimensions_Count
per_column.rationale: A count of sub-dimensions below a threshold, computed from the very ratings that compose the overall score. Highly collinear with and derived from the outcome, hence leakage.

per_column.name: Review_Length
per_column.rationale: A generic, mechanical text-length feature. It lies outside the focus but carries only weak, non-substantive signal; treated as irrelevant per the conservative rule on bare length/token features.

per_column.name: Review_Word_Count
per_column.rationale: Redundant mechanical token count, essentially collinear with Review_Length. Generic surface statistic that does not realise genuine predictive feature engineering.

per_column.name: Is_Premium_Class
per_column.rationale: Derived from the pre-existing Class field but represents an external, causally plausible driver of satisfaction (cabin quality) that is not a component or function of the overall rating. Legitimate predictor.

per_column.name: Traveler_Category
per_column.rationale: Traveller type is an independent contextual attribute plausibly associated with rating differences (e.g., business vs solo expectations) and is not derived from the outcome. Legitimate predictor.

per_column.name: Review_Verified
per_column.rationale: Verification status is external to the rating and can plausibly correlate with rating behavior/credibility. Not a restatement or leak of the focus, so a valid weak predictor.

judge.rationale: Four of the strongest-looking columns (Average_Service_Rating, Service_Consistency, Lowest_Rated_Dimension, Poor_Dimensions_Count) are all deterministic aggregates of the sub-rating dimensions that essentially constitute the Overall Rating, so they leak the focus rather than predict it. Two columns (Review_Length, Review_Word_Count) are generic mechanical text statistics with negligible engineered signal. Only Is_Premium_Class, Traveler_Category, and Review_Verified are legitimate external predictors, and these are mostly light recodings of already-present columns, adding only modest new predictive leverage.
